identity.title: A comprehensive view of the interstellar medium in a quasar host galaxy at z ≈ 6.4

paper_type_evidence.quote: In this work, we present a multi-line study of the star–forming medium in the host galaxy of the quasar PSO J183.1124+05.0926 (hereafter, PJ183+05; R.A.: 12:12:26.97, Dec.: +05:05:33.4) at $z=6.4386$.

question.value: Characterize the global physical properties, gas phases (ionized, neutral, molecular), excitation mechanisms, and mass budget of the star-forming interstellar medium in the quasar host galaxy PSO J183.1124+05.0926 at z=6.4386.

evidence.quote: In this work, we present a multi-line study of the star–forming medium in the host galaxy of the quasar PSO J183.1124+05.0926 (hereafter, PJ183+05; R.A.: 12:12:26.97, Dec.: +05:05:33.4) at $z=6.4386$.

analysis_steps.goal: Model emission lines using analytical first-principles prescriptions and Cloudy simulations

method.value: Solve linear statistical equilibrium equations for level populations in ionized gas and run Cloudy photoionization, PDR, and XDR slab models across grids of density, metallicity, and radiation fields.

evidence.quote: In order to put our observations in the context of the physical properties of the interstellar medium in PJ183+05, we derive analytical predictions based on first principles, and complement them with grids of predicted line ratios using the photoionization code Cloudy (cite: ferland98; ferland13; ferland17).
Namely, we model the ISM as a homogeneous plane-parallel slab of gas exposed to a radiation field.

key_parameters.value: Ionized grid: fixed log U = -2, log n [cm^-3] = [0, +3] (step 0.25 dex), log Z [Z_sun] = [-1, +0.4] (step 0.2 dex), turbulence RMS = 100 km/s, stopping at x_HI = 0.05

evidence.quote: We thus use a fixed log $U$=$-2$ in our analysis.

We assume that the gas volume density is constant within the cloud, and we sample the line emissivity over a range of $\log n$ \[cm$^{-3}$\] $=[0, +3]$ in steps of $0.25$ dex. We assume ISM and PAH grains. The metallicity[^3] in our grids ranges between $\log Z$ \[Z$_\odot$\] $=[-1, +0.4]$ in steps of 0.2 dex.
We also include a CMB background computed at the source’s redshift, and a turbulence with an RMS of 100 km s$^{-1}$. We stop the integration when we reach a ionized fraction of $x_{\rm HI}=0.05$.

key_parameters.value: PDR/XDR grid: log n [cm^-3] = [2, 6] (0.29 dex spacing), log G_0 = [1, 6] (0.29 dex spacing) or log F_X = [-2.0, 2.0] (0.24 dex spacing), log N_H [cm^-2] = [22, 24] (1 dex spacing)

evidence.quote: For the former, we adopt $\log n$ \[cm$^{-3}$\] = \[2, 6\] (0.29 dex spacing). For the latter, we adopt a range of $\log G_0$ = \[1, 6\] (0.29 dex spacing) for PDRs, and $\log F_{\rm X}$ \[erg s$^{-1}$ cm$^{-2}$\] = \[-2.0, 2.0\] (0.24 dex spacing) for XDRs.

findings_qualitative.value: Line velocity profiles across all detected transitions (ionized, neutral, molecular) are consistent at the observed S/N with negligible velocity shifts relative to [C II].

evidence.quote: The velocity profiles of all the detected transitions appear in good agreement at the S/N levels of our observations.

All the detected lines show negligible velocity shifts along the line of sight compared to the rest frame of the galaxy as defined by the \[C ii\] line, with all the velocity shifts, $\Delta v=c\,\delta z / (1+z)$, significantly smaller than the adopted channel width (90 km s$^{-1}$).

claims.hypothesis: What is the main driver of the photoionization budget in the ionized ISM of PJ183+05 (stars vs. the central AGN)?
claims.experiment: Compare the observed [O III] 88 um / [N II] 122 um luminosity ratio against Cloudy and analytical radiative transfer models using black body, SSP, and AGN ionizing templates.
claims.result: The AGN template predicts an [O III]/[N II] ratio ~50 times higher than observed; the observed ratio matches a black body with T_* ~ 25,000 K or an SSP burst age of ~9 Myr.
claims.finding: B-type stars (~15 M_sun) are the main driver of the photoionization budget, and an AGN contribution is not required to explain the ionized gas properties.

evidence.loc: Hardness of the radiation field and metallicity
evidence.quote: The AGN template yields a very high \[O iii\]$_{88\,\mu{\rm m}}$/\[N ii\]$_{122\,\mu{\rm m}}$ luminosity ratio, $\sim 50$ times higher than observed.

evidence.loc: Hardness of the radiation field and metallicity
evidence.quote: The observed line ratio points to a $T_*\approx 25,000$ K for Z=Z$_\odot$, or a burst age of $\approx 9$ Myr.

evidence.loc: Hardness of the radiation field and metallicity
evidence.quote: The observed \[O iii\]/\[N ii\] luminosity ratio points to B-type stars as the main driver of the photoionization budget.

claims.hypothesis: Is the neutral and molecular ISM in PJ183+05 dominated by X-ray Dominated Region (XDR) conditions from the quasar or Photon-Dominated Region (PDR) conditions from young stars?
claims.experiment: Measure CO(7-6), high-J CO (J_up = 15, 16, 19) upper limits, and the [C II] 158 um / [C I] 370 um line ratio, and compare with Cloudy PDR and XDR model grids.
claims.result: High-J CO lines are undetected, and log([C II]/[C I]) = 1.55 (+0.17/-0.13) (or ~15 for the PDR-only [C II] component), which is significantly higher than XDR predictions (<10).
claims.finding: Pure XDR domination is disfavored; the neutral and molecular medium is consistent with a PDR-dominated regime or a combination of PDR and XDR.

evidence.quote: Here we measure a ratio of $\log$ \[C ii\]/\[C i\] = $1.55_{-0.13}^{+0.17}$. Even if we consider only the component of \[C ii\] that is not associated with the ionized medium, \[C ii\]$^{\rm PDR}$, the ratio drops to $\sim 15$, still significantly higher than the predictions for XDRs.

In summary, all these lines of evidence disfavor a scenario in which the neutral and molecular medium in PJ183+05 is dominated by XDR conditions, but leave room for a combination of PDR and XDR, or a PDR–dominated regime.

claims.hypothesis: Does the excitation of water and hydroxyl in PJ183+05 follow typical IR-pumping scaling with total IR luminosity seen in other z > 6 quasars?
claims.experiment: Compare the H2O and OH line luminosities normalized by L_IR as a function of upper level energy against other z > 6 quasars.
claims.result: Detected H2O and OH transitions show line-to-IR luminosity ratios about 3 times higher than in other quasars at similar redshifts, while J_up >= 4 H2O lines are undetected.
claims.finding: Either shocks collisionally excite the H2O and OH levels, or L_IR is underestimated due to an unaccounted hot mid-IR dust component (e.g., AGN torus).

evidence.quote: Strikingly, all of the detected line transitions point to a high H$_2$O- or OH-to-IR luminosity ratio, about 3 times higher than what is observed in other quasars at similar redshifts.
The modest number of transitions observed in our study makes it impossible to draw any robust conclusions on the origin of this discrepancy.

claims.hypothesis: What is the mass budget of the ionized and molecular gas reservoirs in PJ183+05?
claims.experiment: Derive ionized gas masses from [C II] and [N II] level populations and molecular gas masses from dust, CO(7-6), and [C I]+[C II]^PDR.
claims.result: Ionized gas mass is M_HII = (2-3) x 10^10 M_sun; molecular gas mass is M_H2 = 5 x 10^10 M_sun ([C I]+[C II]), 4.5 x 10^10 M_sun (CO), and 8.7 x 10^10 M_sun (dust).
claims.finding: All independent tracers converge on a massive gas reservoir in both the molecular ((0.5-1) x 10^11 M_sun) and ionized ((2-3) x 10^10 M_sun) phases.

evidence.quote: While all the mass estimates rely on uncertain conversion factors (cite: dunne21; dunne22; decarli22), all the methods independently converge towards a massive gaseous reservoir in both molecular \[$(0.5-1)\times10^{11}$ M$_\odot$\] and ionized \[$(2-3)\times 10^{10}$ M$_\odot$\] phase.

why_this_data.value: PJ183+05 has the highest [C II] luminosity among 27 z>6 quasars surveyed in Decarli et al. (2018) and sits at a redshift (z ~ 6.4) where multiple key FIR lines fall into transparent atmospheric windows.

evidence.quote: The \[C ii\] luminosity in this source is the highest among 27 quasars at $z>6$ surveyed in (cite: decarli18), and one of the highest from non-lensed sources currently known at any redshift (cite: pavesi16; tadaki19; andika20; mitsuhashi21).
The quasar resides at a redshift that is convenient for observations of various far-infrared emission lines that fall in transparent windows of the atmosphere at $z\approx 6.4$.

why_this_method.value: Natural weighting and 90 km/s channel binning were chosen to maximize the S/N of line detections while sampling the ~375 km/s line width in ~4 channels; single-pixel extraction was used because the source is spatially unresolved or marginally resolved at >0.7'' resolution.

evidence.quote: We imaged the measurement sets using natural weighting, in order to maximize the signal-to-noise ratio of line detections.

The expected line width ($\sim 375$ km s$^{-1}$ from the analysis of the \[C ii\] data) is thus sampled in $\sim4$ independent channels, while at the same time maximizing the signal-to-noise ratio in the lines.

Two-dimensional channel-by-channel fits of the quasar emission at 88 $\mu$m in the rest-frame revealed that the emission is spatially unresolved or only marginally resolved at $>0.7''$ resolution (cite: venemans20). Therefore, we extracted the spectra of the dust continuum and targeted lines in PJ183+05 on a single-pixel basis.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Simultaneous radiative transfer modeling of dust and molecular gas (Harrington et al. 2021) was rejected because the CO SLED constraints are too sparse.

evidence.quote: While the method by (cite: harrington21) can in principle be applied here, our observational constraints (in particular concerning the CO spectral line energy distribution) are too sparse to lead to informative results.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Applying dust opacity corrections to fiducial line luminosities was rejected due to unknown line-of-sight geometry between gas and dust and its modest impact on final results.

evidence.quote: However, the actual values of such corrections strongly depend on how the line–emitting gas clouds and the dust are distributed along the line of sight, which is unknown. Because of this uncertainty, and due to the modest impact that this correction would have on our final results, we opt not to apply the opacity correction to our fiducial measurements.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Using [O III]/[C II]^ion instead of [O III]/[N II] to constrain radiation hardness was rejected due to large uncertainties on f([C II]^PDR).

evidence.loc: Hardness of the radiation field and metallicity
evidence.quote: We opt to focus on the \[O iii\]/\[N ii\] ratio rather than on the \[O iii\]/\[C ii\]$^{\rm ion}$ ratio because of the uncertainties on $f($\[C ii\]$^{\rm PDR})$ discussed in sec. [4.2](#sec_fpdr).

limitations_admitted.value: The [O I] 63 um line was scheduled but not observed due to unfavorable weather in Cycle 4.

evidence.quote: The \[O i\] 63 $\mu$m line was also scheduled for observations, but unfavorable weather conditions prevented the completion of the program within Cycle 4.

limitations_admitted.value: Modeling the ISM as three distinct homogeneous constant-density components is a crude approximation that ignores spatial and velocity substructure.

evidence.quote: We treat all the emission lines as arising from three distinct components (ionized, neutral, molecular), each described with a simple parametrization (e.g., constant density throughout each cloud). This is clearly a crude approximation that does not capture the complex structure of the ISM in galaxies.

limitations_admitted.value: The PDR fraction of [C II] is highly sensitive to assumed elemental abundances, changing from 0.44 to 0.81 depending on the calibration adopted.

evidence.loc: Inferred [N ii]205 um and the origin of [C ii]
evidence.quote: We point out that this value is highly sensitive to the assumed relative abundances. If we adopt the traditional values from (cite: savage96), we find a much higher $f({\rm [CII]^{PDR}})=0.81$.

limitations_admitted.value: Sparsity of water and hydroxyl transitions prevents an extensive radiative transfer analysis of H2O and OH.

evidence.quote: However, because of the sparsity of the water and hydroxyl transitions studied here, an extensive analysis of the radiative properties of these molecules is beyond the scope of this work.

limitations_admitted.value: Gas mass and SFR estimates rely on uncertain conversion factors, abundance assumptions, and star-formation timescales.

evidence.quote: While all the mass estimates rely on uncertain conversion factors (cite: dunne21; dunne22; decarli22), all the methods independently converge towards a massive gaseous reservoir in both molecular \[$(0.5-1)\times10^{11}$ M$_\odot$\] and ionized \[$(2-3)\times 10^{10}$ M$_\odot$\] phase.

referee_caveats_inferred: Single-pixel spectral extraction across beams ranging from 0.8''x0.7'' (Band 6/8) to 4.0''x3.3'' (Band 3) assumes point-source behavior across all bands; any extended emission beyond ~0.7'' could introduce resolution-dependent aperture bias in line ratios and continuum SED fitting.

The electron density diagnostic relies on [N II] 205 um, which was not actually observed in PJ183+05 but inferred from the empirical LIRG relation of Lu et al. (2015) using the modeled dust color C(60/100).
